title: Stack-hint extraction: broaden matching + add explicit stack_family field from target_intel so #338's augmentation actually fires on live targets
goal: Live Gruyere run 2026-05-19 (3e2cfa5b) confirmed that #338's plumbing works (paths_for_stack returns correct values; orchestrator threads stack_hints) but the NORMALIZER does not match what target_intel actually emits. target_intel produced technology_stack=['Python/AppEngine (Google Frontend server)', 'HTML 4.01 Transitional', 'Custom JavaScript (lib.js)', 'Custom backend application'] — NONE of the keywords in `_STACK_KEYWORD_HINTS` (gruyere, tomcat, rails, django, ...) appear. Result: hints=[], no augmentation, /dump.gtl never probed. The 0/17 problem on the info-disclosure category persists. Two fixes are needed: (a) broaden the keyword table to catch the actual strings target_intel emits (AppEngine, App Engine, Python/, Tomcat/), and (b) update target_intel to emit an explicit `stack_family` field on its asset observation (a single registry-key string, not a free-text description) so normalization isn't necessary in the first place.
scope: Two-part fix: (1) Extend `_STACK_KEYWORD_HINTS` in `workers/runners/_path_augmentation.py` with App Engine, ASP.NET Core, Spring, etc. patterns; review against typical target_intel output catalogue. (2) Update `workers/runners/target_intel/runner.py` to ALSO emit `attributes_json['stack_family']` as a single registry-key string (`python_gruyere` / `aspnet` / `ruby_rails` / etc.) — derived from Claude's response. `stack_hints_from_observations()` prefers this field when present and falls back to the keyword table only when it's missing.
generation_reason: Live run 3e2cfa5b against https://google-gruyere.appspot.com/<instance>/ produced 1 critical + 8 high findings (vs 1 high on the May-18 baseline run) — proves #336 + #337 work empirically. But `info_disclosure_probe` never probed `/dump.gtl` because hints=[] from the normalizer. Without this task, #338's augmentation is structurally complete but empirically inert on live Gruyere. Operator pushback 2026-05-19: 'Dus je weet gewoon niet of het daadwerkelijk werkt? Hoe kun je dan zeggen dat het af is?' — they were right; live test exposed the gap.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Two changes only: broaden normalizer keyword table + add explicit stack_family field to target_intel asset observation. Do NOT add new categories to the path registry. Do NOT change the 5 probe runners. Do NOT touch the orchestrator wiring.
constraints.no_prescriptive_recipes: Per `feedback_no_prescriptive_recipes`: do NOT add hostname-derived shortcuts (e.g. 'if host contains gruyere → python_gruyere'). The hint must come from target_intel's AI analysis of the actual response, not from hardcoded URL patterns. Test `test_no_gruyere_strings_in_module` must continue to pass.
constraints.ai_owns_classification: target_intel's Claude prompt is updated to ask for a stack_family classification using a documented vocabulary (the registry keys). The path-augmentation registry only consumes that classification — it doesn't try to do the classification itself.

success_criteria: target_intel's asset observation now carries attributes_json['stack_family'] = a single registry-key string (or null when unknown).
stack_hints_from_observations() prefers stack_family when present, falls back to keyword table when absent.
Broadened keyword table catches Python/AppEngine, App Engine, ASP.NET Core, Spring Boot, Express.js, Laravel, Symfony patterns commonly emitted by target_intel.
Live re-test against Gruyere: hints contains 'python_gruyere' (verifiable in the orchestrator log line 'AI loop: stack_hints=...').
Live re-test produces a /dump.gtl probe AND an info-disclosure finding flagged HIGH for the Debug Dump content leak.
No regression on the existing 19 #338 test_path_augmentation tests + the target_intel test suite.
must_not_touch: 5 #328-migrated probes (info_disclosure_probe / stored_xss_probe / file_upload_probe / param_pollution_probe / cookie_tamper_probe) — they consume stack_hints unchanged
